text: In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (LED modules on PCB)
test_case: Review test setup per Annex 3: confirm photometric and colorimetric measurements are performed with the LED modules installed in the lamp as supplied; pass if no external/substitute source is used.

text: During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.
applies_to: Photometric test setup for all lamp functions
test_case: Inspect goniophotometer setup per Annex 3: verify masking of surrounding surfaces; pass if no stray reflections contribute to measured intensities.

text: In the case where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one or in a field of different positions the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
applies_to: Lamp installation positions / reference axis
test_case: If multiple mounting positions are declared, repeat photometric measurements at each position or at the extreme positions of the reference axis field; pass if all positions meet paragraph 5 requirements.

text: If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Verify LED modules are operated in steady (continuously lit) mode during intensity measurement; pass if no flashing/pulsed operation used unless specified.

text: In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the distance of measurement shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.
applies_to: Photometric measurement setup
test_case: Check measurement distance against lamp size; confirm intensity scales with inverse square of distance (e.g. compare readings at two distances); pass if inverse-square law holds.

text: In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the measuring equipment shall be such that the angular aperture of the receiver viewed from the reference centre of the light is comprised between 10' and 1 degree.
applies_to: Photometric measurement equipment
test_case: Calculate receiver angular aperture from detector size and distance as seen from the reference centre; pass if between 10' and 1°.

text: In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed to be satisfied if that requirement is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
applies_to: Luminous intensity evaluation for all lamp functions
test_case: For disputed test points, measure within ±0.25° of the nominal direction; pass if requirement is met at a direction within 0.25°.

text: The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp shall be determined. However, in the case of category 5 and 6 direction indicators, the limits of the light emitting surface shall be determined. This requirement shall not apply to rear-registration plate illuminating lamps.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (apparent surface through outer lens)
test_case: Determine and document the apparent surface outline of each function viewed along the reference axis (e.g. luminance imaging or drawing review); pass if limits are defined for each function.

text: Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).
applies_to: Lamp electrical supply during testing (PCB/vehicle connection)
test_case: Measure supply voltage at the lamp connector during photometric tests; pass if 13.5 V (12 V system), 6.75 V or 28 V as applicable.

text: In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
applies_to: Lamp with electronic light source control gear / driver component on PCB
test_case: Operate lamp with the declared control gear/variable intensity control and applicant-specified conditions; pass if test operation matches the applicant's specification.

text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
applies_to: LED modules on PCB without separate control gear
test_case: Operate lamp per applicant-specified voltage/current conditions; pass if test operation matches the declared specification.

text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall on the reference axis (HV) be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement per Annex 3/Annex 8 on both samples at HV; pass if intensity ≥ paragraph 5 minimum for each function.

text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Goniophotometric scan over all visible directions on both samples; pass if no measured intensity exceeds the paragraph 5 maximum for each function.

text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall outside the reference axis be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5 by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Measure all grid points of the Annex 3 light distribution figure on both samples; pass if each point ≥ minimum × percentage (or ≥ specified value).

text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2 be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Measure intensity across the Annex 2 geometric visibility angles on both samples; pass if all values ≥ paragraph 5 minimum (per regulation's specified value).

text: The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Visual examination and intermediate-point measurement per Annex 3 local variation provisions; pass if no intensity between grid directions falls below the Annex 3 threshold.

text: If requested by the applicant to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No.48, in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction, the maximum intensity shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd; this additional test may be conducted taking into account the influence of the vehicle body.
applies_to: Rear position and stop lamp (red light towards front), reversing lamp (optional additional test)
test_case: If requested, goniophotometric scan from 165° to 180° outboard H and -2.5° to +5° V (optionally with vehicle body); pass if max intensity ≤ 0.25 cd.

text: An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamps if designed as interdependent lamp system
test_case: Operate all interdependent lamps simultaneously and perform photometric/colorimetric tests; pass if combined system meets paragraph 5 requirements.

text: If the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility colorimetric and photometric requirement, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s); in this case, the inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed to be satisfied if this (these) interdependent lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device, at all fixed positions of the moveable component(s).
applies_to: Rear position lamp interdependent system split between body and tailgate
test_case: Measure specified interdependent lamp(s) at every fixed position of the movable component (e.g. tailgate); pass if outboard geometric visibility, colour and photometry are met and light distribution field values are met at all positions.

text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
applies_to: Stop lamp / rear position lamp with variable intensity control (if fitted)
test_case: Operate variable intensity control across all its states and measure intensities; pass if all values remain within the paragraph 5 range.

text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp: (a) for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions: under night-time conditions; (b) for other systems: under standard conditions (good visibility, meteorological optical range MOR > 2,000 m, and clean lens).
applies_to: Stop lamp / rear position lamp with variable intensity control (if fitted)
test_case: Set control to night-time (or standard condition) state and measure intensities; pass if ≤ steady luminous intensity maximum of paragraph 5.

text: If a rear position lamp and/or a rear end-outline marker lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp or end-outline marker lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
applies_to: Rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with stop lamp
test_case: Measure intensity with rear position + stop lamp lit together and with rear position lamp alone at all points within ±5° V and ±10° H; pass if ratio ≥ 5:1 at every point.

text: If one or both of the two reciprocally incorporated rear position lamp and stop lamp contain(s) more than one light source and is (are) considered as a single lamp, the values to be considered for the 5:1 ratio are those obtained with all sources in operation.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and stop lamp with multiple LED sources
test_case: For ratio test, energise all LEDs of each function; pass if ratio computed with all sources operating ≥ 5:1.

text: Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Verify luminous intensity compliance testing follows the Annex 8 procedure; pass if test report documents Annex 8 method and results within limits.

text: The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions (light emission through outer lens)
test_case: Colorimetric measurement per function inside the Annex 3 light distribution grid field; chromaticity coordinates within the limits prescribed for the function's colour.

text: To check the colorimetric characteristics of the light emitted, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Apply paragraph 4.8 test procedure (supply/operating conditions) during colour measurement; documented compliance with 4.8 conditions.

text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined in Annex 3, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions; outer lens
test_case: Visual/colorimetric inspection outside the Annex 3 grid field; pass if no sharp colour variation is observed.

text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
applies_to: LED modules on PCB (non-replaceable light sources) of rear position, stop and reversing lamps
test_case: Colour measurement on complete lamp with installed LED modules, per relevant subparagraphs of 4.8; chromaticity within prescribed limits.

text: For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions using more than one light source technology
test_case: Where multiple light source technologies are used in a function, supply each technology separately (samples allowing separate supply) and measure colour per 4.8.1 and 4.8.2; each within prescribed limits.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of rear position lamps (R1, R2, MR) and rear end-outline marker lamps (RM1, RM2) shall meet the requirements in Table 4.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group)
test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1; luminous intensities at all test points within limits of Table 4 for the declared category.

text: For rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps of categories R1, MR or RM1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4∙10^0 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)), the maximum luminous intensity shall be 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp and 8.5∙10^0 cd for a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.) (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)), the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I and Table A2-1 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)), and the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility shall be 5∙10^-2 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)).
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group)
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per 4.8.3.1: minimum ≥ 4 cd, maximum ≤ 17 cd (single) or ≤ 8.5 cd (marked D), distribution per Figure A3-I/Table A2-1, ≥ 0.05 cd within geometric visibility angles.

text: For rear position lamps or rear end-outline marker lamps of categories R2 or RM2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4∙10^0 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)), the maximum luminous intensity shall be 4.2∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp and 2.1∙10^1 cd for a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.) (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)), the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I and Table A2-1 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)), and the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility shall be 5∙10^-2 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)).
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group)
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per 4.8.3.1 across variable intensity range: minimum ≥ 4 cd, maximum ≤ 42 cd (single) or ≤ 21 cd (marked D), distribution per Figure A3-I/Table A2-1, ≥ 0.05 cd within geometric visibility angles.

text: For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
applies_to: Rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with stop lamp
test_case: Photometric measurement with both functions lit; points below 5° down from horizontal ≤ 60 cd; all other points meet Table 4 maximum.

text: Rear position lamps shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group), LED modules on PCB
test_case: Verify failure behaviour of the LED light source per paragraph 4.6.

text: The colour of light emitted by rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps shall be red.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group), outer lens
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of emitted light; chromaticity coordinates within the red boundaries of the applicable colour specification.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of stop lamp supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7 (luminous intensities for stop lamps).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1 of R148; pass if every sample meets all Table 7 values for its category.

text: A stop lamp of category S1 (steady) shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd within the angles of geometric visibility (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a) and (d)).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a) at the required points within the geometric visibility angles of paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d); pass if intensity ≥ 60 cd.

text: A stop lamp of category S1 (steady) used as a single lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60∙10^2 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b)).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement over the full distribution per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if no value exceeds 260 cd.

text: A stop lamp of category S1 (steady) marked "D" (paragraph 3.3.2.5.2.) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.30∙10^2 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b)).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b) of a lamp marked "D"; pass if no value exceeds 130 cd.

text: A stop lamp of category S1 (steady) shall meet the standard light distribution defined in Figure A3-I and Table A2-1, with a minimum luminous intensity of 3∙10^-1 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(c)).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Measure at the grid points of Figure A3-I; pass if values meet the Table A2-1 percentages and are ≥ 0.3 cd.

text: A stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd within the angles of geometric visibility (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a) and (d)).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a) within the geometric visibility angles of paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d); pass if intensity ≥ 60 cd.

text: A stop lamp of category S2 (variable) used as a single lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 7.30∙10^2 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b)).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement in the highest intensity condition per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if no value exceeds 730 cd.

text: A stop lamp of category S2 (variable) marked "D" (paragraph 3.3.2.5.2.) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.65∙10^2 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b)).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement in the highest intensity condition of a lamp marked "D"; pass if no value exceeds 365 cd.

text: A stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall meet the standard light distribution defined in Figure A3-I and Table A2-1, with a minimum luminous intensity of 3∙10^-1 cd (day) and 7∙10^-2 cd (night) (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(c)).
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group)
test_case: Measure at the grid points of Figure A3-I in day and night conditions; pass if values meet Table A2-1 and are ≥ 0.3 cd (day) and ≥ 0.07 cd (night).

text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group); outer lens
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of emitted light (chromaticity coordinates); pass if within the red colour boundaries defined in the regulation.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp of category AR supplied shall meet the minimum luminous intensity of 8.0∙10^1 cd specified in Table 10 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)).
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function group), both samples
test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1. at the reference axis/points of Table 10; pass if luminous intensity ≥ 80 cd on each sample.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp of category AR supplied shall not exceed the maximum luminous intensity of 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the H-plane, as specified in Table 10 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function group), both samples
test_case: Goniophotometric scan of both samples in and above the H-plane; pass if no measured value exceeds 300 cd.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp of category AR supplied shall not exceed the maximum luminous intensity of 6.00∙10^2 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D, as specified in Table 10 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function group), both samples
test_case: Goniophotometric scan of both samples from just below the H-plane down to 5°D; pass if no measured value exceeds 600 cd.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp of category AR supplied shall not exceed the maximum luminous intensity of 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D, as specified in Table 10 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function group), both samples
test_case: Goniophotometric scan of both samples below 5°D; pass if no measured value exceeds 8,000 cd.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp of category AR supplied shall meet the standard light distribution defined in Figure A3-V (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)).
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function group), both samples
test_case: Measure luminous intensity at each grid point of Figure A3-V (Annex 3) on both samples; pass if each point meets the prescribed percentage of the minimum intensity.

text: In the case where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards where a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied.
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function group), when approved for paired installation only
test_case: If the pair-only option is claimed: photometric measurement at 30° inwards on both samples; pass if luminous intensity ≥ 25 cd.

text: Where type approval of the reversing lamp is granted applying the pair-only condition, the device shall only be installed in a pair.
applies_to: Reversing lamp installation on vehicle
test_case: Check approval communication form paragraph 9.1.3. and vehicle installation; pass if the lamp is fitted as one of a pair.

text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function group), LED modules and outer lens
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of emitted light through the outer lens per the regulation's colour test method; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the white colour boundaries.

text: Lamps shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions)
test_case: Conformity of production check: compare production samples against approved type (design, photometry, colour, markings); pass if production lamps match the approved type.

text: The minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 4 shall be complied with.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions)
test_case: Audit of manufacturer's CoP control procedures per Annex 4 (test frequency, records, sampling); pass if all Annex 4 minimum requirements are met.

text: The minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 5 shall be complied with.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions)
test_case: Inspector sampling and photometric testing per Annex 5; pass if samples meet Annex 5 acceptance criteria.

text: For conformity of production, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp photometric performance
test_case: Photometric measurement of production samples at prescribed test points; pass if no value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from prescribed values.

text: For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12 (required minimum 7∙10-1 cd: 5∙10-1 cd equivalent 20 per cent, 3∙10-1 cd equivalent 30 per cent; 6∙10-1 cd: 4∙10-1 cd / 2∙10-1 cd; 3∙10-1 cd: 2∙10-1 cd / 1∙10-1 cd; 7∙10-2 cd: 5∙10-2 cd / 3∙10-2 cd; 5∙10-2 cd: 3∙10-2 cd / 2∙10-2 cd).
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp luminous intensity in the fields of Annexes 2 and 3
test_case: Measure luminous intensity throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3 on production samples; pass if values are not below the Table 12 equivalent 20 per cent (or 30 per cent where applicable per Annex 4/5) values.

text: The rear position lamp (A, R1, R2) shall provide the minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard (shown for a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle). Reduced angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard are used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group), housing, outer lens
test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Part A, Figure A2-I / Table A2-1, with the lamp in its installed position on the vehicle and angles mirrored for the left side. Pass if the light-emitting surface is visible over the full 45°/80° inboard/outboard field, or 20°/80° below the H-plane when the H-plane is below 750 mm.

text: The rear position lamp (A, R1, R2) shall provide the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below. For lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angles are 15° above / 5° below. For optional lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm, the angles are 5° above / 15° below.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group), housing, outer lens
test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Part A, Table A2-1, at the intended mounting height. Pass if the light-emitting surface is visible over the required vertical field: 15°/15°, 15°/5° when the H-plane is below 750 mm, or 5°/15° when the H-plane is above 2,100 mm.

text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall provide the minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard (shown for a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle). Reduced angles of 20° inboard / 45° outboard are used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group), housing, outer lens
test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Part A, Figure A2-I / Table A2-1, with the lamp in its installed position and angles mirrored for the left side. Pass if the light-emitting surface is visible over 45°/45° inboard/outboard, or 20°/45° below the H-plane when the H-plane is below 750 mm.

text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall provide the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below. For lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angles are 15° above / 5° below. For optional lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm, the angles are 5° above / 15° below.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group), housing, outer lens
test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Part A, Table A2-1, at the intended mounting height. Pass if the light-emitting surface is visible over the required vertical field: 15°/15°, 15°/5° when the H-plane is below 750 mm, or 5°/15° when the H-plane is above 2,100 mm.

text: Unless specified otherwise, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits; the direction H = 0° and V = 0° corresponds to the reference axis (on the vehicle horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle and oriented in the required direction of visibility) and passes through the centre of reference.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and stop lamp function groups (photometric light distribution)
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement about the reference axis through the centre of reference; at each grid point compute required value = percentage from Figure x minimum intensity required, rounded down to three significant digits; pass if measured intensity >= computed value.

text: In the case where one of the following lamps is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards: (a) Front and rear direction indicators lamps; (b) Front and rear position lamps; (c) Front and rear end-outline marker lamps; (d) Parking lamps; (e) Stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS; (f) Side marker lamps.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and stop lamp (S1/S2) function groups; mounting height on vehicle
test_case: Check manufacturer-declared mounting height (H plane); if <= 750 mm above ground, verify photometric intensity of rear position and stop lamp only down to 5° below horizontal; pass if all grid points from 5° down upward meet minimum values.

text: Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp function groups (light distribution uniformity)
test_case: Goniophotometric scan of intermediate directions between grid points; pass if each intermediate intensity >= lowest minimum value of the surrounding grid lines.

text: In the case of reversing lamps, if visual examination of a lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, a check shall be made to ensure that no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement is below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
applies_to: Reversing lamp function group
test_case: Visual examination of reversing lamp; if substantial local variations seen, measure intensities between adjacent measurement directions of Figure A3-V; pass if each >= 50 % of the lower of the two prescribed minimum intensities.

text: Front and rear position lamps, parking lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS) and direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c, 12 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8) in the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and stop lamp (S1/S2) function groups
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I grid points; pass if each measured intensity >= percentage of Figure A3-I x minimum intensity from Table 3 (rear position) / Table 7 (stop lamp).

text: Reversing lamps shall meet, at the measuring points expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V, the directions H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the axis of reference (on the vehicle horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle and oriented in the required direction of visibility) and passing through the centre of reference.
applies_to: Reversing lamp function group
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at each Figure A3-V measuring point referenced to the axis of reference through the centre of reference; pass if each measured intensity >= cd value in Figure A3-V.

text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, the differences of mass-produced lamps from the approved type shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (housing, outer lens, retro-reflector, reflector, mechanical and geometric features)
test_case: Dimensional and geometric inspection of production samples against the approved type drawings; pass if deviations stay within inevitable manufacturing tolerances and all requirements of UN R148 are met.

text: With respect to photometric performances, any mass-produced lamp chosen at random shall meet the photometric requirements when tested according to paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Photometric test of randomly selected production lamps according to paragraph 4.8. of UN R148; pass if the results meet the conformity criteria of paragraph 4.8.

text: The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with when the lamp is tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Light colour of rear position, stop and reversing lamps (outer lens, LED modules)
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production lamps under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148; pass if the chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed colour boundaries.

text: For each type of lamp, the holder of the type approval shall carry out at least the tests prescribed in Annex 4, at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production
test_case: Audit of the conformity of production test plan and records; pass if the photometric and colorimetric tests are performed at defined appropriate intervals per UN R148 methods.

text: If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production
test_case: Review of COP records for non-conforming samples; pass if each non-conformity is followed by documented further sampling and testing.

text: The manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production
test_case: Review of corrective action records after non-conformities; pass if documented corrective actions restore production conformity.

text: Tests of conformity shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Check that the COP test plan includes both photometric and colorimetric tests for every function; pass if both are covered.

text: Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp COP testing
test_case: Review of COP test procedures; pass if they follow the UN R148 test methods or approved equivalent methods.

text: Equivalent test methods may be used in conformity tests carried out by the manufacturer only with the consent of the competent authority responsible for approval tests, and the manufacturer shall prove that the applied methods are equivalent to those laid down in this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp COP testing
test_case: Review of authority consent and equivalence evidence (e.g. correlation study) for any alternative method; pass if both are documented.

text: Test apparatus used for conformity tests shall be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a competent authority.
applies_to: Photometric and colorimetric test equipment
test_case: Review of calibration certificates and correlation records; pass if calibration is current and correlation with authority measurements is demonstrated.

text: In all cases the reference methods shall be those of this Regulation, particularly for the purpose of administrative verification and sampling.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp COP testing
test_case: Check that UN R148 methods are designated as reference methods in COP procedures; pass if so.

text: Samples of lamps shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch, a uniform batch being a set of lamps of the same type defined according to the production methods of the manufacturer.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production sampling
test_case: Review of sampling procedure and records; pass if samples are drawn randomly from defined uniform batches of the same lamp type.

text: The conformity assessment shall in general cover series production from individual factories; records concerning the same type from several factories may be grouped only if these factories operate under the same quality system and quality management.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production sites
test_case: Review of COP records per factory; pass if records are per factory, or grouped only for factories under a common quality system and quality management.

text: The sampled lamp shall be subjected to photometric measurements for the minimum values at the points listed in Annex 3 and to measurement of the required chromaticity coordinates.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Measure the luminous intensity at the Annex 3 points and the chromaticity of each sampled lamp; pass if the minimum values and chromaticity coordinates are met and recorded.

text: The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study of the test results and define, in agreement with the competent authority, criteria governing the acceptability of his products in order to meet the requirements for verification of conformity of products in paragraph 6.1. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp COP acceptance criteria
test_case: Review of the statistical analysis and the agreed acceptance criteria; pass if both exist and are agreed with the competent authority.

text: The criteria governing the acceptability shall be such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 5 would be 0.95.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp COP acceptance criteria
test_case: Statistical evaluation of COP test data; pass if a probability of at least 0.95 of passing an Annex 5 spot check is shown at a 95 per cent confidence level.

text: The mass-produced lamps shall conform from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint with the requirements of this Regulation, if any; differences shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (housing, outer lens, retro-reflector, fasteners, mechanical/geometric features)
test_case: Conformity of production check: dimensional and mechanical inspection of lamps chosen at random against the approved type. Pass if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

text: With respect to photometric performance, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation of any mass-produced lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions (LED modules, reflector, outer lens)
test_case: Photometric measurement per paragraph 4.8. on a lamp chosen at random from production. Pass if no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.

text: The chromaticity coordinates of the mass-produced lamps shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Light colour of rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (outer lens, LED modules)
test_case: Colorimetric measurement under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. on lamps chosen at random. Pass if the chromaticity coordinates are within the prescribed colour boundaries.

text: The deviation of any specimen of the four mass-produced lamps selected at random (samples A and B) shall not be more than 20 per cent.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp photometric performance in production
test_case: Annex 5 first sampling: 4 lamps selected at random and marked A (2) and B (2), measured photometrically. Pass if all four deviations are ≤ 20 per cent. Measurement may be terminated if both lamps of sample A show 0 per cent deviation.

text: If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B is more than 20 per cent, the manufacturer shall bring its production in line with the requirements (alignment) before a repeated sampling according to paragraph 3 within two months' time after the notification.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production (manufacturer conformity of production process)
test_case: Verify a corrective action/alignment record exists and that the repeated sampling of 4 lamps (C, D) from stock manufactured after alignment is carried out within two months after notification. Pass if all four C and D deviations are ≤ 20 per cent (P10).

text: For reversing lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
applies_to: Reversing lamp (LED function group)
test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para. 1.2.1. Measure the grid after 1 min and after 10 min of operation. Alternatively, calculate the distribution from the post-stability distribution using the HV intensity ratios at 1 min, 10 min and photometric stability. Pass: all test points are within the min/max values at both times.

text: For all other lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and stop lamp (LED function groups)
test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para. 1.2.2. Measure at 1 min and at either 30 min or photometric stability. The 1 min distribution may be calculated using the HV intensity ratio. Pass: all test points are within the min/max values.

text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the rear position lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after switch ON, with reference coordinate HV (Table A8-1).
applies_to: Rear position lamp
test_case: Per Annex 8 para. 2.1 / Table A8-1. Check the intensities at t = 4 s, measured or calculated from the para. 1 distribution using the HV ratio. Pass: the min/max requirements are met.

text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the stop lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, with reference coordinate HV (Table A8-1).
applies_to: Stop lamp
test_case: Per Annex 8 para. 2.1 / Table A8-1. Check the intensities at t = 0.2 s, measured or calculated from the para. 1 distribution using the HV ratio. Pass: the min/max requirements are met.

text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the reversing lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, with reference coordinate HV (Table A8-1).
applies_to: Reversing lamp
test_case: Per Annex 8 para. 2.1 / Table A8-1. Check the intensities at t = 0.2 s, measured or calculated from the para. 1 distribution using the HV ratio. Pass: the min/max requirements are met.

text: In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (LED modules)
test_case: Confirm that each function uses LED light sources only (review of design and PCB). Pass: the para. 1.2 measurements are compliant, so no additional Table A8-1 time-point testing is required.

text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time, starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Continuous time-resolved intensity measurement from switch ON. Start at 4 s for the position lamp and at 0.2 s for the stop and reversing lamps, and continue until photometric stability. Pass: the minimum intensities are met at all times.

text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
applies_to: Retro-reflector / housing / outer lens (marking area)
test_case: Visual inspection of drawings and samples: a marking space exists that is large enough to accommodate the UI or approval marking plus the 3.3.4.2 markings.

text: All markings on the retro-reflective device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
applies_to: Markings on retro-reflector / lamp
test_case: Visual check of legibility, then a rub/durability test of the markings (e.g. cloth soaked in water and in petroleum spirit); pass if the markings remain legible and intact.

text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value for "a" defined in Table 1; the markings shall be arranged as in the examples in Annex 10.
applies_to: Approval marking
test_case: Measure the marking dimensions against the "a" value in Table 1 and compare the layout with the Annex 10 examples; pass if the dimensions are not below those values.

text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
applies_to: Approval marking on retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection of the marking; pass if a circled "E" with the correct country number is present.

text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
applies_to: Approval marking on retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection; pass if a sequential number of 4 to 6 digits that matches the approval number is present.

text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
applies_to: Approval marking on retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection of the marking layout; pass if the sequential number is adjacent to the circled E.

text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
applies_to: Approval marking on retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection; pass if the class symbol required by paragraph 3.2.5 (e.g. IA or IB) is present and correct.

text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
applies_to: Approval marking on retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection; pass if "150R" followed by the correct two-digit series of amendments is present.

text: If the approval marking defined in paragraph 3.3.2. is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
applies_to: Unique Identifier marking on retro-reflector
test_case: Compare the UI marking with the Figure I format; pass if the format matches and the UI is valid in the UN database (DETA).

text: Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection of the sample; pass if the applicant's trade name or mark is present.

text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, retro-reflective devices shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (Class IA/IB)
test_case: Check whether the retro-reflector's optical design is rotation-dependent; if so, verify that "TOP" is inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface.

text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
applies_to: Retro-reflector markings
test_case: Visual inspection of the device; pass if all required markings are legible on the retro-reflective device.

text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps comply with several UN Regulations and a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed, the marking shall be visible after their installation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (single approval marking)
test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle; pass if the single marking is visible.

text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp: outer lens, retro-reflector, housing
test_case: Design review and disassembly check; pass if every removable light-transmitting part (outer lens, retro-reflector) carries the marking or cannot be removed without removing it.

text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
applies_to: Single approval marking on rear combination lamp
test_case: Measure the mark components and compare them with the minimum sizes required by each applicable regulation (e.g. R150, R148); pass if no component is below the smallest required size.

text: The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the requirements of paragraph 3.5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (production quality system)
test_case: Audit of the manufacturer's COP procedures against the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3); pass if procedures comply.

text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: COP testing of production retro-reflectors against the requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN R150; pass if production samples meet those requirements and conform to the approved type.

text: For retro-reflectors, the minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 2 shall be complied with.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (production control)
test_case: Review of the manufacturer's production control procedures and test records against Annex 2 of UN R150; pass if all minimum requirements are met.

text: For retro-reflectors, the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 3 shall be complied with.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (production sampling)
test_case: Inspector sampling and testing of production retro-reflectors per Annex 3 of UN R150; pass if the samples meet the Annex 3 acceptance criteria.

text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications", and in the Annexes referenced in those sections, of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval shall apply to the retro-reflecting device.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (integrated in rear combination lamp); its installation on M1 vehicle per UN R48
test_case: Review and checklist against UN R48 (M1 vehicle) sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes for rear retro-reflectors, using the series of amendments in force at the application date. Pass if every applicable item is met or justified as not verifiable at device approval.

text: The requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector; intended vehicle category M1
test_case: Identify the R48 provisions pertinent to the rear retro-reflector on M1 vehicles, such as number, colour, geometric visibility angles, position and orientation. Verify the feasible ones at device approval by drawing/CAD review and goniometric visibility check in the intended mounting attitude. Pass if all feasible pertinent requirements are met.

text: Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Design review and execution of the R150 durability/environmental tests (e.g. heat, water penetration, corrosion, fuel and lubricating oil resistance); pass if the retro-reflector meets the photometric and colour requirements after the tests.

text: Retro-reflective devices must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Visual and dimensional inspection of samples against drawings plus design review; pass if no design or manufacturing defects that impair operation or maintenance are found.

text: The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, outer lens, housing, fasteners / clips
test_case: Manual dismantling attempt without tools on the assembled lamp; pass if the retro-reflector components cannot be easily separated or removed.

text: The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
applies_to: Retro-reflector outer surface / outer lens
test_case: Visual inspection and cleaning trial with a cloth on the outer surface; pass if the surface can be cleaned easily.

text: The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances they may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
applies_to: Retro-reflector outer surface / outer lens
test_case: Visual and tactile inspection of the outer surface geometry; pass if the surface is smooth and no protuberance hinders cleaning.

text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, housing, seal / gasket
test_case: Inspection of the assembled lamp as mounted; pass if the retro-reflector inner (reflecting) surface is not accessible without dismantling the device.

text: If retro-reflectors consist of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, they must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (optical unit and filter / outer lens)
test_case: Design review and manual separation attempt under normal use conditions; pass if the optical unit and filter cannot be separated.

text: The colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters by means of paint or varnish is not permitted.
applies_to: Retro-reflector optical unit and filter
test_case: Material specification review and visual/material inspection; pass if colour is obtained by the material itself (e.g. coloured-in-mass) and no paint or varnish is used for colouring.

text: For testing the colour of white, red or amber retro-reflective devices, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1= β2= 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1. shall be used.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (colorimetric test set-up)
test_case: Colorimetric test per R150 para. 4.2.1.2: verify the test set-up uses CIE Standard Illuminant A, 1/3° divergence and β1=β2=0°, or the Annex 4 Part 1 para. 1.1 angle if colourless surface reflection occurs; pass if the set-up conforms.

text: For white, red or amber retro-reflective devices, the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (night-time colour of retro-reflected light)
test_case: Illuminate with CIE Standard Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and β1=β2=0° (or the Annex 4 Part 1 para. 1.1 angle), then measure the x,y chromaticity of the reflected light; pass if the coordinates lie within the UN R48 night-time colour limits for the device colour (red for a rear retro-reflector).

text: For the determination of the luminance factor, the sample shall be tested with the method as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material sample, luminance factor)
test_case: Measure the luminance factor of the retro-reflective sample using the method in Annex 4, Part 2. Pass if the method is applied as described there.

text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection and measurement of shape and dimensions per Annex 5 on all ten samples; pass if every Annex 5 requirement is met.

text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 and colorimetry per paragraph 4.2.1. in the Table 4 test sequence; pass if RI is at or above the Table 3 minima and the colour is within the UN R48 night-time limits.

text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Run the Table 4 sequence (heat, water, fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability in time, weathering); pass if there is no distortion or damage and colour and RI still comply after each test.

text: After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 and, at least one hour after this test, examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Heat test of 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C per Part 1 of Annex 6 on all 10 samples; after at least 1 h, check colour and RI at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if there is no distortion and colour and RI comply.

text: The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values after the heat resistance test shall be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Complete photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 on the min and max samples at all Table 3 angles; pass if every RI value is at or above the Table 3 minima.

text: First group: the two samples shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
applies_to: Retro-reflector, housing, seal / gasket
test_case: Water immersion for 10 min in the normal position and 10 min inverted, then motor fuel for 5 min and oil for 5 min; visual inspection after each step; pass if there is no water penetration or damage and colour and RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0° comply.

text: Second group: the two samples shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Corrosion test of 24 h + 2 h interval + 24 h, then rear-face abrasion test for 1 min; visual inspection; pass if colour and RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0° comply.

text: Third group: the two samples shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Stability in time test per Part 3 of Annex 4, then colorimetry and photometry at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if both comply with 5.1.5. and 5.1.4.

text: The two samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Weathering test per Part 6 of Annex 6, then colorimetry and photometry at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if both comply.

text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Visual colorimetry per paragraph 4.2., with trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt; pass if within the UN R48 night-time red limits.

text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.; the verification shall be performed only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass for red Class IA/IB if RI ≥ 300 mcd/lx.

text: One or more or a range of axis of reference, corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of coefficients of luminous intensity RI, shall be specified for the retro-reflector.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Design documentation review; pass if the axis (or axes or range) of reference is defined.

text: In the case where more than one or a range of different axis of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the photometric measurements shall be repeated making reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Repeat photometry for each specified axis or for the extreme axes of the range; pass if Table 3 minima are met for each.

text: For photometric measurements, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system of the retro-reflective device as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter for Class IA or IB shall be considered, and the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2, though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Mask the device to the declared area within a Ø 200 mm circle and ≤ 100 cm2 during photometry; pass if RI minima are met using only that area.

text: The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area to be used for photometric measurements of the retro-reflector.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Documentation and drawing review; pass if the perimeter of the measured area is defined.

text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA and IB, at an angle of divergence of 20', must be equal to or greater than 3.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 2.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0° and 1.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (red)
test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20' at the listed angles; pass if each RI is at or above the given minimum.

text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA and IB, at an angle of divergence of 1°30', must be equal to or greater than 5∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 2.8∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0° and 2.5∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (red)
test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 1°30' at the listed angles; pass if each RI is at or above the given minimum.

text: RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 are not permissible within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the following lines: (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Scan photometry within the bounded solid angle; pass if no RI value falls below the applicable limit.

text: In the case where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (installation height)
test_case: Confirm the mounting height of the H plane; if < 750 mm, verify RI only down to β1 = -5°; pass if the Table 3 minima are met in the verified range.

text: The testing of the colour for retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Colour measurement per paragraph 4.2.1.; pass if the prescribed method is applied.

text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflector must be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Colorimetry per paragraph 4.2.1.; pass if the chromaticity coordinates are within the UN R48 night-time limits for the declared colour (red for this product).

text: The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (mass production, mechanical/geometric conformity)
test_case: Dimensional and geometric inspection of production samples against the approved type; pass if deviations are within inevitable manufacturing tolerances and the requirements of UN R150.

text: With respect to photometric performances, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if, when testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (photometric performance, CoP)
test_case: Photometric measurement of a randomly selected production retro-reflector per UN R150 methods; pass if no value is more than 20 % below the prescribed minimum values.

text: The chromaticity coordinates of the mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (colour, CoP)
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples per UN R150; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed limits.

text: For each type of retro-reflective device the holder of the approval mark shall carry out at least the conformity tests, at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (manufacturer CoP test programme)
test_case: Audit of CoP plan and records; pass if tests per Annex 2 para. 2.1 are performed at defined intervals for each retro-reflector type using UN R150 methods.

text: If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested, and the manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP non-conformity handling)
test_case: Audit of non-conformity records; pass if additional samples were tested and corrective actions documented for any failing sampling.

text: Tests of conformity shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water of the retro-reflective device.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, outer lens, seal/gasket and housing (CoP test scope)
test_case: Review of CoP test plan; pass if photometric, colorimetric and water penetration resistance tests per UN R150 are included and performed on production samples.

text: Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP test methods)
test_case: Review of test procedures; pass if methods match those of UN R150 or approved equivalents.

text: Where equivalent methods are used in conformity tests carried out by the manufacturer, they shall be used only with the consent of the Type Approval Authority, and the manufacturer shall prove that the applied methods are equivalent to those laid down in this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP alternative test methods)
test_case: Check documented Type Approval Authority consent and equivalence evidence (correlation study) for any non-reference method.

text: Test apparatus used for conformity tests shall be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a Type Approval Authority.
applies_to: Retro-reflector CoP test equipment (photometer, colorimeter, water test rig)
test_case: Audit of calibration certificates and correlation records; pass if calibration is current and correlation with Type Approval Authority measurements is documented.

text: In all cases the reference methods shall be those of this Regulation, particularly for the purpose of administrative verification and sampling.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP reference methods)
test_case: Verify that any dispute/verification testing uses UN R150 reference methods.

text: Samples of retro-reflective devices shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch, a uniform batch being a set of retro-reflective devices of the same type defined according to the production methods of the manufacturer.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP sampling)
test_case: Audit of sampling procedure; pass if samples are randomly drawn from defined uniform batches of the same type.

text: The assessment shall in general cover series production from individual factories; records concerning the same type from several factories may be grouped only if these operate under the same quality system and quality management.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP assessment scope)
test_case: Audit of CoP records; pass if assessed per factory or grouped only for factories under a common quality system and management.

text: The sampled retro-reflective device shall be subjected to photometric measurements at the points and to the chromaticity coordinates provided for in the Regulation, and these shall be measured and recorded.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP photometric/colorimetric measurement)
test_case: Measure CIL at all prescribed angle points and chromaticity coordinates per UN R150 on sampled devices; pass if all points measured and recorded.

text: The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study of the test results and define, in agreement with the Type Approval Authority, criteria governing the acceptability of his products in order to meet the specifications for the verification of conformity of products in paragraph 3.5.1. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP acceptance criteria)
test_case: Audit of statistical analysis and agreed acceptance criteria documentation with Type Approval Authority.

text: The criteria governing the acceptability shall be such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 3 (first sampling) would be 0.95.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP acceptance criteria)
test_case: Statistical evaluation of production test data; pass if probability of passing Annex 3 first sampling is at least 0.95 at 95 % confidence level.

text: The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (mass production: mechanical and geometric conformity)
test_case: CoP inspection: compare mechanical and geometric features of production retro-reflectors with the approved type; pass if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

text: With respect to photometric performance, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if, when testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation; retro-reflective devices with apparent defects are disregarded.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (photometric performance in production)
test_case: CoP photometric measurement of randomly chosen retro-reflectors per R150; pass if no value is more than 20 per cent below the prescribed minimum values.

text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (colour of reflected light)
test_case: CoP colorimetric measurement of production retro-reflectors; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the boundaries prescribed in R150.

text: The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four retro-reflective devices) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both retro-reflective devices of sample A is not more than 0 per cent, the measurement can be closed.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP first sampling)
test_case: First sampling: four randomly selected retro-reflectors (samples A and B, two each) measured photometrically; pass if every specimen deviates by not more than 20 per cent.

text: If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B is more than 20 per cent, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be contested and the manufacturer shall bring his production in line with the requirements (alignment), followed by a repeated sampling according to paragraph 3 within two months' time after the notification.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (production alignment after failed first sampling)
test_case: After failed first sampling, verify production alignment and perform first repeated sampling within two months of notification.

text: The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples C and D (all four retro-reflective devices, selected from stock manufactured after alignment) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both retro-reflective devices of sample C is not more than 0 per cent, the measurement can be closed.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP first repeated sampling)
test_case: First repeated sampling: four retro-reflectors from post-alignment stock (samples C and D); pass if every specimen deviates by not more than 20 per cent.

text: If the deviation of one specimen of samples C or D is more than 20 per cent but the deviation of all specimens of these samples is not more than 30 per cent, the manufacturer shall again bring his production in line with the requirements (alignment) and a second repeated sampling according to paragraph 4 shall be carried out within two months' time after the notification.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (production alignment after failed first repeated sampling)
test_case: Check deviations of samples C and D: >20 per cent but all ≤30 per cent triggers realignment and second repeated sampling within two months.

text: If the deviation of one specimen of samples C and D is more than 30 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 shall be applied.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP first repeated sampling, withdrawal criterion)
test_case: First repeated sampling: any specimen deviating by more than 30 per cent = fail, approval withdrawn.

text: The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples E and F (all four retro-reflective devices, selected from stock manufactured after alignment) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both retro-reflective devices of sample E is not more than 0 per cent the measurement can be closed.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP second repeated sampling)
test_case: Second repeated sampling: four retro-reflectors from post-alignment stock (samples E and F); pass if every specimen deviates by not more than 20 per cent.

text: If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be contested, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 shall be applied.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (CoP second repeated sampling, withdrawal criterion)
test_case: Second repeated sampling: any specimen deviating by more than 20 per cent = fail, approval withdrawn.
