text: One of the retro-reflectors of sample A after the sampling procedure in paragraph 2 shall be tested according to the procedure described in paragraph 1 of Part 2 of Annex 6 or, in the case of the Advance Warning Triangle, the sample A shall be tested according to the procedure described in paragraph 2 of Part 2 of Annex 6; the retro-reflectors shall be considered acceptable if the test has been passed, and if the test on sample A is not complied with, the two retro-reflective devices of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure and both shall pass the test.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (resistance to water penetration in production)
test_case: Water penetration test per Annex 6 Part 2 paragraph 1 on one retro-reflector of sample A; pass if test passed; otherwise both sample B devices tested and both must pass.

text: When the RI of a retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Annex 4 Part 1: at β1 = β2 = 0°, turn the device slightly while monitoring RI. Pass: the presence or absence of a mirror effect is determined and recorded.

text: If any mirror effect is produced when the retro-reflective device is slightly turned at β1 = β2 = 0°, a reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Annex 4 Part 1: if a mirror effect is found, measure RI at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°. Pass: this reading is used in place of the 0°/0° value and meets the paragraph 5 requirement.

text: With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI, which must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (not marked TOP)
test_case: Goniophotometer at β1 = β2 = 0° (or the paragraph 5 angle) and α = 20': rotate the device about its reference axis and find minimum RI. Pass: minimum RI ≥ the paragraph 5 value.

text: When the RI of a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP" is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to the value of ε of minimum RI; if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (not marked TOP)
test_case: Measure RI at all specified illumination and divergence angles at the ε of minimum RI, using up to ±5° rotation if needed. Pass: specified RI values are attained.

text: With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°, and the RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (marked TOP)
test_case: Goniophotometer at β1 = β2 = 0° (or the specified angle), α = 20': rotate ±5° about the reference axis. Pass: RI ≥ prescribed value at every position.

text: If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Measure RI at β1 = β2 = 0°, ε = 0°. If RI ≥ 150% of the specified value, perform all further measurements at ε = 0°. Pass: all values meet requirements at ε = 0°.

text: The CIE-angular system as shown in Figure A4-I shall be used for specifying and measuring retro-reflective device and marking materials.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Review of the test set-up and report. Pass: angles are defined and set according to the CIE co-ordinate system of Figure A4-I.

text: For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Verify the source calibration certificate. Pass: the source is CIE Standard Illuminant A and the measurement follows Annex 4 Part 1.

text: In the measuring geometry for retro-reflective devices, the angular diameter of the source shall be δ ≤ 10'.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Calculate δ from the source size and the measuring distance. Pass: δ ≤ 10'.

text: In the measuring geometry for retro-reflective devices, the angular diameter of the measuring device shall be γ ≤ 10'.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Calculate γ from the receiver's largest dimension and the measuring distance. Pass: γ ≤ 10'.

text: In the measuring geometry for retro-reflective devices, the angular diameter of the illuminated area shall be η ≤ 80'.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Calculate η from the largest dimension of the retro-reflector's illuminating surface and the measuring distance. Pass: η ≤ 80'.

text: The measuring distance shall be chosen in such an order that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η given in Figure A4-III are respected, but not lower than 10 m.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Measure the test distance. Pass: distance ≥ 10 m and the δ, γ and η limits are met.

text: The illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform, the variation complying with max/min ≤ 1.05 when checked with a measuring element whose sensitive area is not greater than one-tenth of the area to be examined.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Scan the illuminance over the useful area with a sensor of ≤ 1/10 of that area. Pass: Emax/Emin ≤ 1.05.

text: The photometer head shall be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency for the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Check the photometer V(λ) correction certificate. Pass: the head is corrected to the CIE photopic observer.

text: The photometer head shall not show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within the area of its aperture; otherwise suitable provisions shall be added, e.g. the application of a diffusing window at a certain distance in front of the sensitive surface.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Check the spatial uniformity of the photometer aperture. Pass: no perceptible variation, or a diffusing window is fitted.

text: In the photometry of retro-reflection, the field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Inspect the set-up for apertures and masks. Pass: the field of view and the light spread are restricted.

text: Reflections from the floor and walls which occur over the relatively long test distances used shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector photometric test set-up
test_case: Inspect the photometric range. Pass: baffles screen the sample and the photometer head from floor and wall reflections.

text: The residual stray light value, measured when the sample is covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape or a specular black surface suitably oriented with a light trap, shall be subtracted from that measured on the retro-reflective device.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Measure the reading with the sample covered by a black cover. Pass: this value is subtracted from each retro-reflector reading in the test report.

text: For testing the daytime colour and luminance factor of the retro-reflective material, illumination by CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0) shall be used.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material)
test_case: Review test setup: confirm D65 illumination and 45a:0 (annular/normal) geometry used for daytime colour and luminance factor measurement; pass if both are applied.

text: Daytime colour measurements shall be done with a spectrophotometer in accordance with the provisions of Publication CIE 15:2004, either illuminated poly-chromatically or with a monochromator providing stepwise the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) at an angle 45° to the normal and viewed along the normal (geometry 45/0).
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material)
test_case: Verify spectrophotometer setup per CIE 15:2004 with D65 at 45° incidence and normal viewing (45/0); pass if configuration matches.

text: When a monochromator providing stepwise the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 is used for daytime colour measurement, the stepwise resolution Δλ shall be not larger than 10 nm.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material)
test_case: Check monochromator step setting; pass if Δλ ≤ 10 nm.

text: If similar simulation spectra are used instead of D65, it shall be verified that the colorimetric measuring procedure is of the same accuracy, the quality of the D65 simulation being assessed by the method described in ISO 23603:2005(E)/CIE S 012/E:2004.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material)
test_case: Review D65 simulator assessment report per ISO 23603:2005(E)/CIE S 012/E:2004; pass if equivalent accuracy is demonstrated.

text: The spectral distribution of the Illuminant used for daytime colour measurement shall be in category BC (CIELAB) or better.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material)
test_case: Check illuminant quality category per ISO 23603; pass if category BC (CIELAB) or better.

text: The measurement area for daytime colour measurement shall be at least minimum 4.0 cm².
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material)
test_case: Measure sampling aperture area; pass if ≥ 4.0 cm².

text: The apertures of the light source and the receiver shall have sufficient dimensions in proportion to distances to ensure compliance with the CIE 15 recommendations for 45°a:0° geometry (irradiation between cones of 40° and 50° half angle; collection within a cone of 5° half angle).
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material)
test_case: Review instrument geometry: illumination uniformly between 40° and 50° half-angle cones and receiver collection within 5° half-angle cone about the normal; pass if aperture dimensions achieve these angles.

text: The luminance factor βv,R of the retro-reflective material shall be determined by relating the luminance L of the sample to the luminance L0 of a perfect diffuser of known luminance factor under identical conditions of illumination and observation, or, where the colour of fluorescent material has been colorimetrically determined in compliance with paragraph 1, by the ratio of the tristimulus value Y of the sample to the tristimulus value Y0 of the perfect diffuser.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (retro-reflective material)
test_case: Measure L and L0 (or Y and Y0) under identical 45a:0 D65 conditions and compute βv,R; pass if determination follows the prescribed method.

text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of retro-reflective devices of Class IA or IB shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (Class IA/IB) integrated in the rear combination lamp, illuminating surface shape
test_case: Visual inspection (Annex 5, para. 3.3) of the retro-reflector illuminating surface from an observation distance of 10 m; pass if its shape cannot easily be confused with the equilateral triangle shape of Class IIIA/IIIB retro-reflectors (para. 2.1).

text: In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (moulded plastics reflector, e.g. Class IA/IB)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 1 para. 1 heat resistance test: condition the retro-reflector sample in a dry atmosphere oven at 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 consecutive hours; verify the conditioning duration and temperature are recorded within tolerance.

text: In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, after the 48-hour heat exposure the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (moulded plastics reflector, e.g. Class IA/IB)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 1 para. 1: after 48 h at 65 °C, cool the sample for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C before examination; verify cooling time and temperature are within tolerance.

text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component must be visible.
applies_to: Retro-reflector, in particular its optical component
test_case: Visual examination after completion of the Annex 6 Part 1 heat resistance test procedure; pass if no cracking and no appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device or its optical component is visible.

text: Retro-reflective devices whether part of a lamp or not, or a sample unit of retro-reflective marking, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (integrated in rear combination lamp)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: strip all removable parts and immerse the device for 10 min in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C, with the top of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. Record the setup; then apply the criteria of para 1.2/1.3.

text: The water immersion test of retro-reflective devices shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (integrated in rear combination lamp)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: invert the device 180° and immerse for 10 min at 50 °C ± 5 °C, with the rear face about 20 mm under water. Confirm the sequence is completed.

text: The retro-reflective device sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (integrated in rear combination lamp)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1: immediately after the 50 °C immersions, immerse under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C. Verify the transfer is immediate and the temperature is within tolerance.

text: After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
applies_to: Retro-reflector optical unit / housing seal
test_case: After the Annex 6 Part 2 para 1.1 sequence, inspect visually. Pass: no water on the reflecting surface.

text: If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
applies_to: Retro-reflector optical unit
test_case: Visual inspection after immersion. Any clearly visible water at the reflecting surface means fail.

text: If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, in the case of retro-reflectors, the RI shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
applies_to: Retro-reflector photometric performance (RI)
test_case: Lightly shake the device to remove external water, then measure RI per para 5.1.3.2.2 of UN R150. Pass: RI meets the requirements referenced in that paragraph.

text: As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests of Annex 6 Part 3 shall be applied to retro-reflective devices of the Classes IB and IIIB to assess resistance to water penetration.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (Class IB/IIIB) incorporated in rear combination lamp
test_case: Manufacturer elects alternative procedure; perform moisture test (Annex 6 Part 3 para 2) and dust exposure test (para 2.3) instead of the standard water penetration test.

text: For the moisture test, the water spray cabinet shall be equipped with a nozzle(s) which provides a solid cone water spray of sufficient angle to completely cover the sample device, with the centreline of the nozzle(s) directed downward at an angle of 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of a rotating test platform.
applies_to: Retro-reflector moisture test setup
test_case: Verify nozzle spray covers the whole device and nozzle centreline angle is 45° ± 5° to the platform vertical axis.

text: For the moisture test, the rotating test platform shall have a minimum diameter of 140 mm and rotate about a vertical axis in the centre of the cabinet.
applies_to: Retro-reflector moisture test setup
test_case: Measure platform diameter ≥ 140 mm and confirm central vertical rotation axis.

text: The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min as measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform, the collector having a height of 100 mm and an inside diameter of a minimum of 140 mm.
applies_to: Retro-reflector moisture test setup
test_case: Calibrate spray with 100 mm high, ≥140 mm ID collector centred on platform axis; rate within 2.5 to 4.1 mm/min.

text: For the water spray test, the sample device shall be mounted on a test fixture with its initial RI measured and recorded before being subjected to the water spray.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Measure and record initial RI of mounted retro-reflector before spray exposure.

text: During the water spray test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp housing, seal/gasket, drain openings
test_case: Inspect that no openings are taped or sealed and drain wicks are fitted during the spray test.

text: During the water spray test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp with retro-reflector
test_case: Verify platform rotation speed of 4.0 ± 0.5 rpm throughout test.

text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF during the water spray test.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions grouped with retro-reflector; LED modules on PCB
test_case: Energise lamp functions at design voltage with 5 min ON / 55 min OFF cycle during spray; check cycle log.

text: The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp with retro-reflector
test_case: Run spray test for 12 h comprising 12 cycles of 5 min ON / 55 min OFF.

text: After the water spray test, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp with retro-reflector
test_case: Stop spray and rotation; allow 1 h drain with cabinet door closed.

text: Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation and no standing pool of water shall be formed, or be able to be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp housing, outer lens, seal/gasket
test_case: Visual inspection of interior after drain; tap and tilt device; pass if no standing pool of water forms.

text: After the drain period, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Dry exterior with dry cotton cloth; measure RI per Annex 4 Part 1 and compare with initial RI and applicable requirements.

text: The interior of the dust exposure test chamber shall be cubical in shape, 0.9 to 1.5 m per side, with an internal volume (not including a "hopper shaped" bottom) of 2 m3 maximum, charged with 3 to 5 kg of the test dust, and capable of agitating the test dust by means of compressed air or blower fans so that the dust is diffused throughout the chamber.
applies_to: Retro-reflector dust exposure test setup
test_case: Verify chamber dimensions 0.9–1.5 m per side, volume ≤ 2 m3, dust charge 3–5 kg, and agitation system diffusing dust throughout.

text: The test dust used shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
applies_to: Retro-reflector dust exposure test
test_case: Confirm test dust certificate conforms to ASTM C 150-84 fine powdered cement.

text: For the dust exposure test, the sample device shall be mounted on a test fixture with the initial RI measured and recorded before exposure to dust.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Measure and record initial RI of mounted retro-reflector before dust exposure.

text: During the dust exposure test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp housing, seal/gasket, drain openings
test_case: Inspect that no openings are sealed and drain wicks are fitted during dust test.

text: The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall, and devices with a length exceeding 600 mm shall be horizontally centred in the test chamber.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp with retro-reflector
test_case: Measure distance to chamber walls ≥ 150 mm; centre horizontally if device length > 600 mm.

text: The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, and the dust shall be allowed to settle between the agitation periods.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp with retro-reflector
test_case: Run 5 h exposure with 2–15 s agitation every 15 min and settling between; check controller log.

text: Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Clean and dry exterior with dry cotton cloth; measure RI per para 5.1.3.2.2 and compare with initial RI and applicable requirements.

text: Retro-reflective devices shall be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Corrosion test per Annex 6 Part 4 (ISO 9227:2017 saline mist); verify photometric (RA) and colorimetric characteristics remain within prescribed limits after test.

text: The resistance of the front surface of the retro-reflective device to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked; the testing of resistance to corrosion is described in ISO Standard 9227:2017.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (front surface and rear face protection)
test_case: Saline mist test per ISO 9227:2017; inspect front surface for tarnishing and rear face protection for deterioration.

text: The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp with integrated retro-reflector
test_case: Remove all removable parts; expose to saline mist 24 h, dry 2 h, expose 24 h (total 50 h); record compliance with test sequence.

text: In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (if containing essential metal components, e.g. metallised reflector)
test_case: Verify salt spray chamber at 35 °C ± 2 °C using 5 % NaCl solution in distilled water with ≤ 0.02 % impurities.

text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp with integrated retro-reflector
test_case: Visual inspection immediately after 50 h saline mist test; pass if no excessive corrosion liable to impair device efficiency.

text: The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: After 48 h recovery, measure RA per Annex 6 Part 2 at β2 = 5°, α = 20'; pass if RA ≥ Table 9 value and ≤ Table 10 value.

text: Before measuring the coefficient of retro-reflection after the corrosion test, the surface shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Verify retro-reflector surface is cleaned of salt deposits prior to post-corrosion RA measurement.

text: For the resistance test of the accessible rear face of mirror-backed retro-reflective devices (moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA), the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (mirror-backed, accessible rear face)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 5: brush the entire reverse side of the retro-reflector with a hard nylon brush. Pass: brushing is performed as the first step of the sequence before solvent exposure.

text: After having brushed, in the case of moulded plastics reflectors as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, the rear face of the retro-reflective device, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute; the cotton cloth is then removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (mirror-backed, accessible rear face)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 5 / Annex 7 Part 1: apply a cotton cloth soaked in the specified mixture to the brushed rear face for 1 minute, remove the cloth and let the device dry. Pass: exposure carried out for the full 1 minute.

text: As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with the same brush as before.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (mirror-backed, accessible rear face)
test_case: Annex 6 Part 5: once the solvent has fully evaporated, brush the reverse side again with the same hard nylon brush. Pass: second brushing completed with the same brush.

text: The RI of the retro-reflective device shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector (mirror-backed, accessible rear face)
test_case: Cover the whole mirror-backed rear face with Indian ink, then measure the RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. Pass: RI meets the requirements of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.

text: The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013, shall be capable to control temperature and relative humidity and shall be equipped with a water spray system.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (weathering test set-up)
test_case: Check the test apparatus against EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013. Pass: temperature and relative humidity control and a water spray system are present.

text: The water spray system of the accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be capable to spray a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (weathering test set-up)
test_case: Measure the spray quantity per unit area over 5 minutes. Pass: at least 0.3 ml/cm².

text: The spray water used in accelerated artificial weathering shall be in accordance to the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (weathering test set-up)
test_case: Verify the spray water quality against EN ISO 4892-2:2013. Pass: the water conforms.

text: The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1: TM1 (Black-standard thermometer, cycle No. 1) of 102 min dry at 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) / 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm), 65 ± 3 °C black-standard temperature and 50 ± 10 % relative humidity, followed by 18 min water spray at 60 ± 2 W/m² / 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m²; or TM2 (Black-panel thermometer, cycle No. 4) with the same parameters at 63 ± 3 °C black-panel temperature.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Run the Xenon-arc exposure per EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using either TM1 or TM2 cycle parameters from Table A6-1, and record which method was used. Pass: irradiance, temperature, humidity and spray cycle are held within the stated tolerances under equilibrium conditions.

text: In case of retro-reflective devices, the samples shall be exposed to accelerated artificial weathering for a period of 500 hours.
applies_to: Retro-reflector
test_case: Expose retro-reflector samples per Table A6-1. Pass: the total exposure duration is 500 hours.

text: Preparation of test specimens for accelerated artificial weathering shall be in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (test samples)
test_case: Review the specimen preparation against the EN ISO 4892-2:2013 general guidelines. Pass: the preparation conforms.

text: For the resistance to fuels test of a retro-reflective device, a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (outer surface / illuminating surface)
test_case: Annex 7 Part 1: Prepare the test mixture of 70 vol. % n-heptane and 30 vol. % toluol. Check the mixture composition against the test record. Pass if the specified mixture is used.

text: The outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (outer surface / illuminating surface)
test_case: Annex 7 Part 1 para. 1.1(a): Lightly wipe the outer surface, in particular the illuminating surface, with a cotton cloth soaked in the 70/30 n-heptane/toluol mixture. Pass if the procedure is carried out as specified.

text: After about five minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (outer surface / illuminating surface)
test_case: Annex 7 Part 1 para. 1.1(b): Inspect the wiped surface visually about 5 minutes after wiping. Pass if there are no apparent surface changes; slight surface cracks are acceptable.

text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangles of type 1, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil, and after about 5 minutes the surface shall be cleaned.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (outer surface / illuminating surface)
test_case: Annex 7 Part 2 para. 1.1: lightly wipe the outer surface, especially the illuminating surface, with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil. Wait about 5 minutes, then clean the surface. Pass: procedure applied as specified before the photometric check.

text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangles of type 1, after the lubricating oil exposure and cleaning, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (photometric performance after oil resistance test)
test_case: After the oil wipe and cleaning per Annex 7 Part 2 para. 1.1, measure the coefficient of luminous intensity (RI) per para. 5.1.3.2.2. Pass: RI meets the values required by para. 5.1.3.2.2.

text: The approval number shall be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
applies_to: Approval marking on the retro-reflector / rear combination lamp
test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark on the device against Annex 10 Figure A10-I and paragraph 3.3.; pass if the approval number is adjacent to the circle surrounding the "E".

text: The digits constituting the approval number shall face the same way as the "E".
applies_to: Approval marking on the retro-reflector / rear combination lamp
test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark; pass if the approval number digits have the same orientation as the letter "E".

text: The group of symbols indicating the class shall be diametrically opposite the approval number.
applies_to: Approval marking on the retro-reflector (class symbol, e.g. IA, IB)
test_case: Visual inspection of the approval mark per Annex 10 Figure A10-I; pass if the class symbol group is positioned diametrically opposite the approval number relative to the circle surrounding the "E".

text: The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
applies_to: Installation of the rear combination lamp (housing, fasteners/clips, seal) on the vehicle, including rear position, stop, reversing lamp functions and retro-reflector
test_case: Inspect installation on vehicle and perform vibration exposure representative of normal conditions of use (paras 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1., 2.3.10.2.); afterwards re-verify photometric, colour and geometric visibility/position characteristics; pass if all remain within the prescribed values of the Regulation.

text: It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.
applies_to: Mounting and fastening of the rear combination lamp (housing, fasteners/clips) on the vehicle
test_case: Inspect mounting design and attempt to shift lamp orientation under normal handling/service (e.g. tailgate operation, cleaning, vibration); pass if lamp aim/position cannot change unintentionally without deliberate use of tools.

text: For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, rear retro-reflector)
test_case: With the vehicle on a flat horizontal surface, measure the angle between the reference axis of each fitted lamp function and the bearing plane; pass if parallel within ±3°.

text: The reference axis of signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, rear retro-reflector)
test_case: Measure the angle in plan view between the reference axis of each fitted lamp function and the vehicle median longitudinal plane; pass if parallel within ±3°.

text: For the orientation of the reference axis of light-signalling devices when fitted to the vehicle, a tolerance of ±3° shall be allowed in each direction.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation (reference axis orientation)
test_case: Verify measured deviations of the reference axis from the prescribed orientation, vertically and horizontally; pass if each deviation is no more than 3°.

text: Any specific instructions as regards fitting of the light-signalling device laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation (housing, fasteners/clips, seal/gasket)
test_case: Inspect the installed lamp against the manufacturer's fitting instructions (mounting, orientation, fastening); pass if all instructions are met.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and, in the case where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.
applies_to: Installation on vehicle: rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector mounting height and orientation
test_case: Place the M1 vehicle unladen (per paras 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1., 2.3.10.2.) on a flat, horizontal surface, with any AFS in neutral state; measure the mounting height and orientation of each rear lamp function and retro-reflector; pass if the measured values meet the installation requirements specified for each function.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).
applies_to: Installation of the left and right rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions and rear retro-reflector) on the vehicle
test_case: Measure the left and right lamp positions relative to the vehicle median longitudinal plane, using the exterior geometrical form of the housing and lens on vehicle or CAD. Pass if the positions are mirror-symmetric about the plane.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
applies_to: External form of the left-hand and right-hand rear combination lamps (housing, outer lens, retro-reflector)
test_case: Compare the external geometry of the LH and RH lamps (CAD mirror check or visual inspection), ignoring the interior structure. Pass if the external forms are mirror images about the median longitudinal plane.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions and retro-reflector of the LH/RH pair (outer lens, LED light sources)
test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function on the LH and RH lamps per the applicable device regulation colorimetric method. Pass if both lamps of each pair meet the same colour requirement (red for rear position, stop and retro-reflector; white for reversing).

text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
applies_to: Photometric performance of the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions and retro-reflector of the LH/RH pair
test_case: Perform goniophotometric measurement of each function on the LH and RH lamps at the prescribed test points. Pass if the light distributions are substantially identical, unless the pair is approved as a matched pair.

text: In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle and only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the front of the vehicle.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp, if it incorporates a manufacturer logo (outer lens / light-emitting area)
test_case: Inspect the vehicle rear (and front) for lamps incorporating logos. Pass if there are at most two lateral logos (one per side) or one central logo on each end.

text: In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp, if it incorporates a logo (outer lens / light-emitting area)
test_case: Inspect any logo incorporated in the lamp. Pass if every logo is a vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logo.

text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical the above requirements (paragraphs 5.1 to 5.5 of UN R48, including symmetrical installation of paired lamps) shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
applies_to: Installation of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflector) on the vehicle
test_case: Installation inspection per UN R48: on a vehicle with asymmetrical external shape, verify the lamp positions, symmetry and geometric visibility requirements of the preceding paragraphs are met as far as the body shape allows; deviations shall be justified by the asymmetry only.

text: Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions and retro-reflector in a single housing)
test_case: Design review and installation inspection on the vehicle: verify each grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated function separately meets its colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility and electrical connection requirements of UN R48. Pass if all are met.

text: The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Photometric and colorimetric measurement of each function with all other functions of the rear combination lamp switched OFF. Pass if each function meets its prescribed intensity and colour limits.

text: When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.
applies_to: Rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with stop lamp (or other function) sharing the outer lens / LED modules
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of each reciprocally incorporated function (e.g. stop lamp) with that function and the rear position lamp switched ON together. Pass if the chromaticity coordinates stay within the prescribed colour boundaries.

text: Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are not permitted to be reciprocally incorporated.
applies_to: Stop lamp function
test_case: Design review of the lamp: check that the stop lamp does not share a light source or illuminating surface with any direction-indicator lamp. Pass if no reciprocal incorporation exists.

text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that: (a) either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis. These requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions with an apparent surface of two or more distinct parts (LED modules behind the outer lens)
test_case: CAD/geometric measurement of the apparent surface projection in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the outer lens. Pass if projected area ≥ 60 % of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or the minimum distance between facing edges of adjacent distinct parts ≤ 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.

text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that: (a) either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
applies_to: Lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors forming a single lamp (retro-reflector, lamp functions if marked "D")
test_case: Geometric measurement on the vehicle installation in the direction of the reference axis. Pass if projected apparent surfaces ≥ 60 % of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or the minimum distance between facing edges ≤ 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.

text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
applies_to: Rear lamp functions forming a single lamp per 2.4.11.1.(d)
test_case: Apply the geometric verification of paragraph 5.7.2.1 (≥ 60 % quadrilateral occupation or ≤ 75 mm gap between facing edges). Pass if either criterion is met.

text: Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system; however, a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.
applies_to: Housing and outer lens containing multiple lamp functions / apparent surfaces
test_case: Design and approval documentation review: verify lamps sharing the housing or common outer lens are not declared/approved as an interdependent lamp system unless band- or strip-shaped. Pass if classification is consistent.

text: The maximum height of the lamp above the ground shall be measured from the highest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
applies_to: Installation of rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector (height above ground)
test_case: Vehicle on substantially horizontal ground. Measure from the ground to the highest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis. Pass if the value is within the maximum height limit for each function. Exact edges need not be determined where compliance is clear.

text: The minimum height of the lamp above the ground shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
applies_to: Installation of rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector (height above ground)
test_case: Vehicle on substantially horizontal ground. Measure from the ground to the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis. Pass if the value is at or above the minimum height limit for each function. Exact edges need not be determined where compliance is clear.

text: For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
applies_to: Installation height of rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector where reduced geometric visibility angles are claimed
test_case: Determine the H plane through the centre of reference of each lamp function. Measure its height above the ground with the vehicle on horizontal ground. Pass if any reduced vertical visibility angle applied matches the H-plane height condition in the Regulation.

text: The position of the lamp as regards width, when referred to the overall width, shall be determined from that edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is the furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
applies_to: Lateral installation position of rear position lamp, stop lamp and retro-reflector (distance to the vehicle's outer edge)
test_case: Measure from the outermost edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle's overall width. Pass if within the limit for each function. Exact edges need not be determined where compliance is clear.

text: The position of the lamps as regards width, when referred to the distance between lamps, shall be determined from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
applies_to: Lateral installation position of paired rear position lamps, stop lamps and retro-reflectors (separation distance between lamps)
test_case: Measure the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of the paired lamps in the direction of the reference axis. Pass if at or above the minimum separation for each function. Exact edges need not be determined where compliance is clear.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions (LED modules, PCB driver, outer lens)
test_case: Functional and photometric check: switch each function ON at nominal voltage and monitor luminous intensity, colour and apparent surface over the ON period (e.g. goniophotometer/photometer recording, colorimeter, visual inspection). Pass if no intentional variation (no dimming patterns, flashing, colour change or change of illuminated area) occurs while the function is ON.

text: The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary (a) in relation to the ambient light, (b) as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or (c) when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions (any intensity variation implemented by LED driver/PCB)
test_case: For each implemented variation mode (ambient-light dependent, other lamps ON/OFF, e.g. stop lamp with rear position lamp ON, or other function use), measure photometric characteristics (intensity at grid points, colour) per the applicable device regulation in every state. Pass if all states meet the technical provisions for the lamp concerned (e.g. min/max intensities, colour, intensity ratios); if no variation is implemented, verify by design review.

text: Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and stop lamp (red functions) as installed on the vehicle rear
test_case: Vehicle installation check per paragraph 5.10.4.1 (Annex 4, Zone 1, 25 m in front of vehicle); pass if no red light from the rear lamp is visible from the front.

text: For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
applies_to: Rear position lamp and stop lamp (red functions), outer lens and housing as installed on the vehicle
test_case: Observer moving within Zone 1 of Annex 4 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle; pass if the apparent surface of the red lamp is not directly visible.

text: In case of doubt, the requirement of paragraphs 5.10.4.1 and 5.10.4.2 shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp red functions (rear position and stop lamp) and outer lens
test_case: Photometric measurement during lamp type approval of red light intensity emitted towards the front, accounting for vehicle body influence if applicable; pass if ≤ 0.25 cd per lamp.

text: The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously, except while one or more of the following conditions exist (paragraph 5.11.1): (a) front and rear position lamps, as well as side-marker lamps when combined or reciprocally incorporated with said lamps, are switched ON as parking lamps; (b) side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators; (c) daytime running lamps are switched ON; (d) front position lamps function is substituted under the provisions of paragraph 5.12.1.
applies_to: Rear position lamp function group; vehicle wiring connection to the PCB / electrical connector
test_case: Vehicle-level inspection and functional check of the lighting circuit: operate the position lamp switch and verify that the rear position lamps switch ON and OFF only together with the front position lamps, end-outline marker lamps (if any), side-marker lamps (if any) and rear registration plate lamp. Check that independent switching occurs only under exceptions (a) to (d). Pass if no other independent switching is possible.

text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp function groups if designed as an interdependent lamp system; LED modules on PCB and wiring
test_case: If the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system (e.g. split between body and tailgate), operate each function and observe all LED light sources of all interdependent lamps. Pass if all light sources of the system switch ON and OFF simultaneously.

text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
applies_to: Reversing lamp (function group), outer lens, LED modules
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light with the reversing lamp energised; pass if the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) lie within the white boundaries defined in the Regulation.

text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
applies_to: Stop lamp (function group), outer lens, LED modules
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light with the stop lamp energised; pass if the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) lie within the red boundaries defined in the Regulation.

text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group), outer lens, LED modules
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light with the rear position lamp energised; pass if the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) lie within the red boundaries defined in the Regulation.

text: The colour of the light reflected by the non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be red.
applies_to: Retro-reflector (rear retro-reflector, non-triangular)
test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the reflected light under the standard illuminant; pass if the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) lie within the red boundaries defined in the Regulation.

text: The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
applies_to: Installation of rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions and rear retro-reflector on the vehicle
test_case: Inspection of the vehicle installation: count the installed rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors and compare them against the numbers specified in the individual specifications of UN R48 (paragraph 6). Pass if each count equals the prescribed number.

text: Any lamp may be installed on movable components provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector), where any function is mounted on a movable component such as a tailgate
test_case: Installation review on the vehicle: identify whether any lamp function is fitted on a movable component (e.g. tailgate). If so, verify compliance with paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. Pass if all conditions of those paragraphs are fulfilled, or if no lamp is installed on a movable component.

text: Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and rear retro-reflector installation on movable components (e.g. tailgate)
test_case: Installation inspection on vehicle: with the movable component in each fixed position (closed and every fixed open position), verify position, geometric visibility, colour and photometric values of the rear position lamp and retro-reflector; pass if all requirements are met in every position.

text: In the case where the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D" (see paragraph 2.4.11.1.), only one of the lamps needs to meet the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable components.
applies_to: Rear position lamp / rear retro-reflector realised as two lamps marked "D" on movable components
test_case: Check lamp marking "D"; with the movable component in each fixed position, verify that at least one of the two lamps meets position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements; pass if satisfied in all positions.

text: Where additional lamps for the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator and rear retro-reflector functions are fitted and are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
applies_to: Additional rear position lamps / retro-reflectors on fixed body compensating for lamps on movable components
test_case: Open the movable component to each fixed open position; verify the additional lamps are switched ON and meet position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps on the movable component; pass if all met.

text: In the case where the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of paragraph 5.18.1. shall be satisfied; however, additional lamps for the above functions may be switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, provided that these additional lamps satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
applies_to: Rear position lamp realised as interdependent lamp system entirely on movable component
test_case: With the movable component in every fixed position, verify the interdependent system meets position, geometric visibility, colour and photometry (para 5.18.1), or that switched-ON additional lamps meet all these requirements in fixed open positions; pass if met.

text: In the case where the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, with the exception of direction indicator lamps, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
applies_to: Rear position lamp realised as interdependent lamp system split between fixed body and movable component
test_case: Identify interdependent lamp(s) specified at device approval; with the movable component in every fixed position, verify position, outwards geometric visibility, colour and photometry; pass if all met.

text: For an interdependent lamp system partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, the inwards geometric visibility requirement(s) is(are) deemed to be satisfied if the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant still conform(s) to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
applies_to: Rear position lamp interdependent lamp system split between fixed body and movable component (inwards visibility)
test_case: Photometric measurement in the field of light distribution of the specified interdependent lamp(s) at every fixed position of the movable component; pass if prescribed device-approval photometric values are met.

text: When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp functions (rear position, stop, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) if installed on a movable component (e.g. tailgate/boot lid)
test_case: Installation inspection per UN R48: place the movable component (e.g. tailgate open) in each position other than the normal position of use, operate the lamp functions and verify by visual assessment that no glare or undue discomfort is caused to road users; pass if no undue discomfort is observed.

text: When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector), if mounted on a movable component such as a tailgate
test_case: With the lamp fitted on the movable component (e.g. tailgate), open and close the movable component repeatedly to its normal position(s) of use; after each cycle, measure the lamp position and orientation relative to the vehicle. Pass: the lamp returns each time to the manufacturer-specified position(s), and installation and geometric visibility requirements are still met in that position.

text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use" (fixed position meaning the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not).
applies_to: Rear position lamp and rear retro-reflector installation on vehicle (e.g. if mounted on tailgate or other movable component)
test_case: Installation inspection: place each movable component carrying or near the lamp in every manufacturer-specified fixed (rest) position other than normal position of use; measure the visible fraction of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; pass if no more than 50 per cent is hidden.

text: If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and retro-reflector on movable component; additional compensating lamps and their activation
test_case: Move the movable component to each fixed position where more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface is hidden; verify additional lamps switch ON automatically and that they comply with position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements of the replaced lamps.

text: If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable and additional lamps per paragraph 5.21.1 are not provided, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road, for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.
applies_to: Vehicle with rear position lamp on movable component (user notice)
test_case: Inspect vehicle for presence and content of the user notice describing the positions of the movable components and the need to warn other road users; pass if present and correct.

text: The alternative of paragraph 5.21.2 (communication form remark and user notice) shall not be applied to retro-reflectors; retro-reflectors shall comply with paragraph 5.21 or paragraph 5.21.1.
applies_to: Rear retro-reflector
test_case: Design review: verify that retro-reflector occlusion by movable components is resolved by compliance with 5.21 (max 50 per cent hidden) or by additional retro-reflectors per 5.21.1, not by a user notice.

text: With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse; the lamp shall therefore be capable of being made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions (LED modules on PCB, vehicle wiring connection); not applicable to the retro-reflector
test_case: Installation inspection on vehicle: with the lamp installed and connected to the vehicle wiring, verify that each function (rear position, stop, reversing) operates when activated without any action other than fitting a light source and/or fuse; pass if all functions operate, otherwise the lamp is deemed not present.

text: Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation on vehicle (applies only if any function uses a replaceable UN R37 light source; LED modules on PCB used as non-replaceable light sources are excepted)
test_case: Review the light source type of each function; if R37 replaceable sources are used, perform a practical replacement on the installed lamp using only the vehicle-supplied tools and following the manufacturer's procedure. Pass if a non-expert can correctly replace the light source without special tools.

text: For lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., the vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement.
applies_to: Vehicle documentation / owner's manual for the rear combination lamp (if R37 replaceable light sources are used)
test_case: Documentation check: verify the vehicle-supplied documentation contains a detailed light source replacement procedure for the lamp. Pass if the procedure is present, detailed and matches the actual replacement steps.

text: In the case where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.
applies_to: LED light source modules on PCB (if they include a holder for an R37 replaceable light source)
test_case: Design review of the light source modules for any R37 holder; if present, perform the replacement test of paragraph 5.23 on the installed lamp. Pass if the R37 light source can be correctly replaced without expert assistance and without special tools other than those supplied with the vehicle.

text: Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (function group) – fail-safe replacement function, if implemented
test_case: Simulate failure of the rear position lamp function (e.g. disconnect LED string); verify by photometric and colorimetric measurement and inspection that the replacement function's colour, main intensity and position are similar to the failed rear position lamp function.

text: Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement device remains operational in its original safety function.
applies_to: Replacement device (e.g. stop lamp function group) used for fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp
test_case: With the rear position lamp function failed and replacement active, operate the replacement device's original function (e.g. apply brake); verify that it still performs its original safety function and complies with its photometric requirements.

text: During temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.
applies_to: Vehicle installation – dashboard tell-tale / failure detection signal from rear combination lamp electronics
test_case: Vehicle-level test: induce rear position lamp failure triggering replacement; verify that the dashboard tell-tale activates and indicates the temporary replacement and need for repair throughout the replacement.

text: If rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, the intensity of all these lamps shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (R2) and stop lamp (S2) function groups with variable intensity control
test_case: Photometric measurement of each function across the variable intensity range. Pass if all functions vary simultaneously, in the same direction and in a similar proportion.

text: For rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions in the entire intensity range.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (R2) and stop lamp (S2) intensity control
test_case: Measure the intensities of the rear position lamp and stop lamp simultaneously during intensity transitions over the full range. Pass if the prescribed stop/position intensity ratio is maintained at all points.

text: The increase and decrease of the luminous intensity of variable intensity lamps shall respond only to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds or contamination of the light emitting surface, and shall stay within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations.
applies_to: Variable intensity control of rear position lamp and stop lamp
test_case: Review the control logic and simulate each environmental condition. Pass if variation is triggered only by the listed conditions and the measured intensities stay within the minimum and maximum limits of the pertinent UN Regulations.

text: Independent from environmental conditions, a decrease of the luminous intensity of variable intensity lamps, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, shall only be activated when the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal to or less than 20 m. An intensity decrease already activated may remain active only as long as the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 50 km/h.
applies_to: Variable intensity control logic (traffic conditions)
test_case: Vehicle or HIL test with simulated speed and following distance. Pass if the decrease activates only at ≤20 km/h or ≤20 m, is cancelled once speed exceeds 50 km/h, and the intensity stays within the regulatory limits.

text: Stop lamps of category S4 and rear fog lamps of category F2 may produce variable luminous intensity, based on the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., independently from the other lamps.
applies_to: Stop lamp function group (if category S4)
test_case: Review the category and control logic. Pass if any independent variation of an S4 stop lamp is based only on the conditions in 5.26.1 and 5.26.2.

text: No sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition of variable luminous intensity lamps.
applies_to: Rear position lamp and stop lamp variable intensity transitions
test_case: Time-resolved photometric recording during intensity transitions. Pass if no abrupt step change in intensity is observed.

text: For vehicles of M and N categories, the electric power supply conditions for the devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. shall comply with the provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1. to 5.27.3. when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant; the applicant shall demonstrate this to the Technical Service responsible for type approval testing.
applies_to: Electrical supply to the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (LED modules on PCB, vehicle wiring connection)
test_case: Vehicle-level demonstration: operate the vehicle electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition representative of the M1 category as specified by the applicant. Measure the voltage at the rear combination lamp terminals for each function. Pass if the provisions of 5.27.1 to 5.27.3 are met.

text: The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp terminals / connector (rear position, stop, reversing functions), where approved at a special supply or requested voltage
test_case: With the vehicle in a constant voltage operating condition, measure the voltage at the lamp terminals for each function. Pass if the voltage is ≤ the voltage stated in the lamp's type approval documentation. Not applicable if the exemption in 5.27.3 applies.

text: In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent. The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp terminals / connector (rear position, stop, reversing functions)
test_case: With the vehicle in a constant voltage operating condition, measure the voltage at the device terminals. Pass if the voltage is ≤ 6.95 V (6 V system), ≤ 13.905 V (12 V system) or ≤ 28.84 V (24 V system). Not applicable if the exemption in 5.27.3 applies.

text: The provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1. and 5.27.2. shall not apply to devices which include: an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp LED modules / PCB driver electronics
test_case: Design review of the lamp's electronics and type approval documentation. Determine whether the device includes an electronic light source control gear, an integrated variable intensity control, or only UN R128-approved light sources. If so, the voltage limits of 5.27.1 and 5.27.2 do not apply; otherwise verify them per 5.27.1 or 5.27.2.

text: There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; however, no account is taken of obstacles if they were already presented when the lamp was type-approved.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp installation (rear position, stop, reversing lamps and retro-reflector) on vehicle
